description: Evidence on how often San Francisco's commuters go to work on an average weekday: BATS 2023's stated frequency against its travel diaries, with BART's day-of-week counts and office-attendance series. Assembled for the choice of the model's commuting rate (METHOD.md, Commuting days).

bats2023Stated.note: Typical days a week, workers who commute; the model applies it with the ACS 2024 share working from home (21.4%) and a 7% absence allowance: 0.606 per worker not working from home, 0.470 per full-time worker of the synthetic population (22.5% of them work from home).

bats2023Diary.source: MTC BATS 2019-2023 dashboard (Tableau workbook mtc_BATS_2019_2023_Dashboard.twbx, extract Summary_TripRate_TripDistance, 'By Commute Category and County'); full-time workers' weighted travel days by commute category
bats2023Diary.weightedDays: Tuesday-Thursday only (BATS 2023 Final Report, Notes for data users: 'only Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday days were weighted')
bats2023Diary.note: In 2019 the diaries put 29% of San Francisco's full-time workers' Tuesday-Thursday days in 'did not work', when the ACS put 7% of them working from home: the category undercounts commuting even before the pandemic.

bartDayOfWeek2025.source: BART hourly origin-destination file date-hour-soo-dest-2025.csv.gz (data/beta3/raw/obs), weekday dates of 2025 excluding holidays; exits at Embarcadero, Montgomery, Powell, and Civic Center by entry hour 6-10am
bartDayOfWeek2025.note: Tuesday-Thursday mornings carry 16% more commuters into downtown than the average weekday; Friday 37% fewer. A Tuesday-Thursday diary therefore overstates an average weekday's commuting, not understates it.

kastleSF.source: Kastle Back to Work Barometer, SF metro, weekly occupancy vs Feb 2020 (reference/backcast-inputs.json)

officeAttendance.sfControllerQ1_2026: Office of the Controller, Status of the San Francisco Economy, May 15, 2026: 2026 office attendance slightly above 2025 levels (Kastle); downtown BART exits at a post-pandemic high (charts only).
officeAttendance.bayAreaCouncil: Bay Area Council Economic Institute, Bay Area Return to Office survey (employers), February 2025: 25% of employees in the office five days a week, 63% hybrid (most three to four days), 11% fully remote; 3.0 days a week on average, against 2.3 in late 2021.
officeAttendance.bartGrowth: BART exits at the city's eight stations, July-August 2024 to 2026: +28.9% (downtown four +31.4%) (reference/backcast-inputs.json)

reading: The diaries' 32% is a Tuesday-Thursday figure, the busiest days, and their own 2019 figure (56%) shows the category undercounting commutes; corrected by the 2019 ratio to a plausible pre-pandemic rate (about 86% of full-time workers' days: ACS 2019 working from home 7%, absence 7%) and spread over Monday-Friday by BART's day-of-week pattern, it gives about 0.43 for fall 2023, against the stated frequency's 0.47; office attendance and BART have risen since. The model's counts are the other test (commute-basis.json).
